newsitem.title: MEXICO: Autoparts boosts Desc's Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Autoparts boosts Desc's Q2 earnings.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Desc S.A. reported positive first half earnings boosted by strong autoparts sales, analysts said on Tuesday.
Second quarter revenues and operating profits grew 16.5 and 16 percent in real terms, compared with the year-ago quarter, although net earnings were down due to non-cash items.
Net earnings of 956.33 million pesos for the first half were slightly above an average of 938 million forecast by analysts in a previous Reuters survey.
Alexis Panton, an analyst with Caspian Research, said strong sales reported sales were an encouraging sign that offset the fall in net earnings.
"Earnings looked good, especially in the autoparts and agribusiness divisions and point the way to improved sales and margins in future," he said.
Desc's earnings could look even better in the upcoming quarters if the peso were to weaken slightly, Panton said.
"If the peso softens a little, it will be good for Desc. Sales could increase by 16-20 percent in the next quarter," he added.
Scott Kolb, an analyst with the Banorte brokerage, Desc's earnings were, "very much in line with projections, backed up by strong performance from autoparts."
Sales by the autoparts division totaled 2.943 billion pesos in the first half, up 25.9 percent from year-ago figures.
Kolb added that improved prices could bolster earnings by the chemicals division in the third quarter.
Daniel Goldstein of ING Barings said Desc's earnings showed the company was, "very solid and managed very conservatively."
The analysts agreed Desc's real estate division continued to be a disappointment. In the first half, net earnings by the division fell 82.6 percent in real year-on-year terms to 8.8 million pesos.
((--Tomas de la Rosa, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7912))
